The block is a synthetic, reversible communication intervention inspired by the planarian octanol studies. Ticks are not calibrated biological hours. Voltage color contrast is amplified for visibility. The model uses fixed hand-designed spatial rules plus a compact learned correction; this demo is not a biological prediction.

A memory of signals.
A choice of anatomy.

The tissue state tracks physical matter, synthetic voltage, biochemical activity, regulatory and axis fields, structure, fast and slow edge memory, delayed communication, and induction memory. A cut removes cells and their incident connections while preserving the state of surviving tissue.

Technical details

A 254-parameter PyTorch checkpoint supplies the learned rates and small local residual. Explicit synthetic rules set wound growth, an axial chart retained in cells, organizer thresholds, voltage response, eye placement, and fast-to-slow connection consolidation. The browser runs a JavaScript port of the recurrent transition with the exported weights; no Python service or synthetic teacher is called during inference.

The three panels show one current state, including the regulatory, polarity, and structural channels separately selectable in the third panel. The target reference is displayed for comparison only.

What the demo shows.
What it cannot claim.

↗

Normal control

The intact precursor develops a normal synthetic one-head, one-tail planarian. A trunk fragment can regenerate under untreated and brief-block conditions.

SYNTHETIC DEMO
↗

Sustained broad block

In the tested Python protocol, sustained middle-band broad coupling block creates a posterior organizer that survives washout and a clean recut. The brief and half-dose protocols are negative controls.

TESTED PROTOCOL
○

Biological interpretation

Voltage colors, tick durations, organizer thresholds, and structural memory are synthetic modeling assumptions. These outputs do not validate a drug response or predict real planarian regeneration.

LIMITATION

The browser transition passed a numerical comparison with Python (maximum error 3.65 × 10⁻⁷), and the protocol branches passed a held-out synthetic test. View validation details ↗
